page.layout: One column of running text, with a centred heading block (CONCIO XXXV., Eccles. 19.) before the second passage. The woodcut ornament stands at the start of the first sentence of that passage. No marginal notes. Running head at top, page number at top left.

main_text.p: Legitur de Zenone Cittieo, quòd ipse simul & Cleanthes assedederint Chæremonidæ. At ille quum sentiret affectum amoris, furrexit. Hoc admirante Cleanthe, etiam à bonis, inquit, medicis audio, aduerius inflationes optimum esse remedium quietem. Subduxit se vir integerrimus imminenti periculo. Filius castissimæ virginis, autorque vitæ ac optimus medicus Iesus Christus sanctificet corda nostra, & auertat oculos nostros, ne videant vanitatem, & illuminet mentes nostras, vt cernant veritatem, quæ nos verè liberos reddat, & in nobis regem, vinum, & mulieres vincat, Amen.
main_text.head: CONCIO XXXV.
Eccles. 19.

p.i: Perarius ebriosus non ditescet, & paulatim sublabetur, qui spernit exigua. Vinum & mulieres etiam cordatos auferunt (sugillantq; sapientes:) & qui consuevit meretricibus, euadit confidentior. Caries & vermes occupabunt eum, & anima confidens auferetur (grauiq; suppli-cio contabescet.)

main_text.p: 1 Duo grauissimi morbi iam passim grassantur, quos sanare vult Sapiens his verbis. Alter vocatur Ebrietas, alter Fornicatio.

page.notes: The woodcut ornament at the start of the italic passage is not text. The hyphen after "suppli" is printed as a dot at the line end and is copied as a hyphen. "Eccles. 19." is set apart on its own line and treated as a verse reference. Otherwise the text is clear; no doubtful readings.
